prompt: Which of these is a claim title?

choices.text: Orders by region in 2024 and 2025, as a percentage change on the year before
choices.why: That is a label: it names the data.

choices.text: North grew fastest, at four times Southeast's rate
choices.why: Right. A sentence with a verb and the finding.

choices.text: Figure 3
choices.why: A number, not a title.

choices.text: Regional analysis of Horta's orders over the last two years
choices.why: That names a method, not a finding.

prompt: Why is a claim title more honest than a label title?

choices.text: Its claim is in the open, for checking
choices.why: Right. The reader holds it against the chart and agrees or objects.

choices.text: It contains more words
choices.why: Length is not honesty.

choices.text: It cannot be wrong
choices.why: It can be wrong, which is exactly why it is worth stating.

choices.text: It removes the need for axis labels and a source line
choices.why: Axes still need their units.

prompt: A scatter plot shows sales rising with the number of employees per shop. Which title stays true to it?

choices.text: Hiring staff increases sales
choices.why: That claims a cause the chart cannot show.

choices.text: Stores with more staff sold more
choices.why: Right. It states what the data shows, without claiming a cause.

choices.text: Staff and sales, by store
choices.why: True, but a label; it states no finding.

choices.text: Our best stores have the best people
choices.why: Neither "best" is measured by the chart.

prompt: Where does a direct label go on a line chart?

choices.text: In a box in the top right corner, inside the frame
choices.why: That is a legend.

choices.text: Under the horizontal axis, beside the tick labels
choices.why: That is where the axis labels go.

choices.text: At the right-hand end of each line
choices.why: Right, where the eye arrives.

choices.text: In the title
choices.why: The title states the finding; the names go on the lines.

prompt: When is a legend still the better choice?

choices.text: Two lines that end far apart on the right-hand side
choices.why: That is the easiest case for direct labels.

choices.text: A bar chart sorted from longest to shortest bar
choices.why: The axis already names the bars.

choices.text: Hundreds of points in two groups
choices.why: Right. Labelling each point is impossible.

choices.text: A single line
choices.why: One line needs a title, not a legend.

prompt: Besides saving the reader a lookup, what does a direct label do that a legend cannot?

choices.text: It makes the chart more colourful and easier to remember
choices.why: Colour is not its contribution.

choices.text: It lets the title be shorter and plainer
choices.why: The title is a separate decision.

choices.text: It works without telling colours apart
choices.why: Right. Lesson 14's reason.

choices.text: It fixes the axis range
choices.why: Labels do not change axes.

prompt: What must every value axis say?

choices.text: What is measured, and its unit
choices.why: Right: "delivery time (minutes)".

choices.text: The name of the software used
choices.why: Readers do not need it.

choices.text: Every single value in the data
choices.why: Four to six ticks are enough.

choices.text: The date the chart was made
choices.why: That belongs in the source line, if anywhere.

prompt: Where does the lesson put a vertical axis's title?

choices.text: Beside the axis, rotated 90 degrees
choices.why: That is the default, and it makes the reader tilt their head.

choices.text: Above the axis, horizontal
choices.why: Right, at the top left where the eye starts.

choices.text: In the legend
choices.why: The legend names series, not axes.

choices.text: Nowhere; units are obvious
choices.why: Units are never obvious to the reader.

prompt: Why does a chart need a source line?

choices.text: To fill the space at the bottom
choices.why: It is not decoration.

choices.text: Because the law requires it on every chart
choices.why: The reason is checkability, not law.

choices.text: To credit the designer
choices.why: The source names the data, not the designer.

choices.text: So the numbers trace back to where they came from
choices.why: Right. A chart that cannot be checked asks to be believed.

prompt: What is a reference line for?

choices.text: A value to measure the data against
choices.why: Right, such as 15,000 orders a month.

choices.text: To replace the vertical axis
choices.why: The axis stays; the line adds a benchmark.

choices.text: To decorate empty space
choices.why: It carries a meaning or it should go.

choices.text: To show where the data was cut
choices.why: That would be a gap, marked differently.

prompt: Northeast first led South in July 2024, fell back, and led for good three months later. Which title is true of the story?

choices.text: Northeast overtook South in July 2024
choices.why: True of one month, false of the story: it fell back.

choices.text: Northeast and South are level
choices.why: By December 2025 Northeast was well ahead.

choices.text: Northeast overtook South in October 2024
choices.why: Right. October is when it stayed ahead.

choices.text: South overtook Northeast in 2025
choices.why: The reverse of what happened.

prompt: How many annotations does the lesson suggest on one chart?

choices.text: One per data point
choices.why: That buries the chart.

choices.text: None; annotations are clutter
choices.why: Well-chosen annotations explain moments the reader would wonder about.

choices.text: As many as fit
choices.why: Space is not the limit; attention is.

choices.text: Two or three
choices.why: Right. More, and they compete.

prompt: Southeast grew 14.6% and the company 25.9%. How many percentage points below the company is Southeast, to one decimal place?
How is twenty thousand five hundred and eighty-six written for a Brazilian reader?

choices.why: Right. A point separates thousands in Portuguese.
That is the English convention, read as twenty point five in Portuguese.
A space and a decimal that is not needed.
No separator, and an English decimal point.

prompt: A chart labels one bar 60.5% and the next 14%. What is wrong?

choices.text: Percentages should not appear on bars
choices.why: Values on bars are fine.

choices.text: The precision is inconsistent
choices.why: Right. Keep one precision across the chart.

choices.text: 14% should be written 0.14
choices.why: A percentage is clearer for readers.

choices.text: Nothing is wrong
choices.why: Mixed precision makes the numbers look unequal in certainty.

prompt: Every piece of text in this chart is drawn as a stroke. Find each kind.
hint: The source sits at the very bottom.

prompt: Match each piece of chart text to its job.

pairs.right: says what, where, when and in what unit
names a mark where it is
explains one moment in the data

prompt: Put the text of a chart in the order a reader meets it.
Southeast's growth was 11.3 percentage ___ below the company's.
